findings.title: Directory junction/symlink traversal escapes workspace confinement in local effect seams
findings.component: src/environments/local.ts absolute()/resolveReal() (pre-fix), used by fs read/write, search reads, exec cwd, mkdir/stat
findings.preconditions: Attacker-controlled repository or workspace contains a directory symlink/junction (e.g. created on Linux/macOS or by tooling) pointing outside; model proposes an in-workspace-looking path under it
findings.reproduction: audit/security-2026-10/tools/repro-junction-escape.mts — gate returned allow, putFile wrote OUTSIDE the workspace; readFile/exec-cwd escaped likewise
findings.expected: All effect seams fail closed with PathEscapeError; nothing lands outside the canonical workspace root
findings.actual_pre_fix: Lexical resolve() allowed the path; effects followed the junction and escaped
findings.impact: Complete defeat of the workspace boundary for reads, writes and command working directories
findings.root_cause: Confinement compared lexical paths; ancestors were not canonicalized
findings.remediation: absolute() now realpaths the deepest existing ancestor, compares against the canonical real root, and rejects Windows aliases (ADS, trailing dot/space, drive-relative)

findings.title: No Host/Origin validation — DNS-rebinding can read console token and drive API
findings.preconditions: Operator visits a malicious page while the server runs; page rebinds its hostname to 127.0.0.1
findings.reproduction: curl -H 'Host: evil.example.com' http://127.0.0.1:3131/ → 200 (pre-fix); token is embedded in that HTML
findings.expected: Requests with non-loopback Host or foreign Origin are rejected
findings.actual_pre_fix: Accepted; token-bearing console served to any Host; no Origin checks at all
findings.impact: Token theft + full API control via the operator's browser
findings.root_cause: HTTP trust boundary relied on loopback binding alone
findings.remediation: Host allowlist and Origin allowlist enforced before routing; verified 403 on spoofs, 200 on loopback

findings.title: Ledger open-guard falsely reports 'journal corruption' on any continued mission; blocks resume
findings.preconditions: Mission received a directive after mission.closed (first-class continuation) — routine in web console use
findings.reproduction: POST /missions/:id/directive on closed mission (200) → POST /missions/:id/resume → 500 'journal corruption at seq N: prev-hash-mismatch' while verifyChain()=OK (verify-closed-mission-journal.mts proves the chain is intact)
findings.expected: Continuation is legitimate; reopen/resume works; genuine tampering still fails closed
findings.actual_pre_fix: Guard demanded closure be the last record, contradicting the product's own continuation records
findings.impact: False tamper alarms, resume impossible, trust erosion in the integrity layer
findings.remediation: Guard now checks only that the closure receipt's chainTip binds to the closure record's prevHash; forged/invalid post-closure records still fail via verifyChain (test)
regression_tests: F-07 continuation opens cleanly + forged record fails

findings.title: Console served without security headers (no CSP / frame denial / nosniff)
findings.reproduction: curl -D - / → no CSP, no X-Frame-Options, no nosniff
findings.impact: Approval actions clickjackable; no containment if any XSS is ever introduced; sniffing ambiguity
findings.remediation: CSP (self + inline, frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'none'), X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, no-store added; UI verified for zero CSP violations under real Edge

findings.title: Latent DOM-XSS sinks (raw error strings into innerHTML; unescaped missionId in inline handlers; unvalidated deep-link id)
findings.severity: Low (latent — not currently reachable with attacker characters)
findings.confidence: High for sink presence; Medium on exploitability (server error bodies probed: fixed strings, no echo)
findings.remediation: escapeHtml on error paths; data-attribute + getAttribute pattern for receipt buttons; ULID validation for ?missionId deep-links
findings.regression: covered by UI e2e + escaping now enforced at each sink

findings.title: Attached interpreter-eval flag forms bypass R4 detection
findings.reproduction: grant argv-prefix ["node"] + proposal ["node","-eprintln(1)"] was allowed without escalation
findings.remediation: Attached short-flag and --flag=value forms now detected; bare prefix still matches plain `npm test` (regression-tested)

findings.title: IPv6 host-pattern cross-matching
findings.reproduction: grant hosts ["[::1]"] matched any bracketed IPv6 host (split(':')[0] === '[')
findings.remediation: Bracket-aware host extraction in both copies

findings.title: Windows canonicalization aliases accepted by confinement
findings.reproduction: 'weird.'/'weird ' aliased onto 'weird'; 'C:evil.txt' resolved to ws\evil.txt; ADS rejected late at rename (EINVAL) with direct-write fallback path untested for ADS targets
findings.remediation: All alias classes rejected up-front (folded into F-03 fix)

not_findings: Trailing space in Authorization header accepted (HTTP OWS trimming — normalization, not a bypass)
Crafted mission ids in URLs (404 bodies never echo attacker strings)
Hostile onerror goal stored and rendered (escaped; playwright: no dialog, no injected elements)
Package tarball: no .env values, no .forge state, no audit artifacts
